name: Iron City No. 1 Power Generator and Compute Center

profile.reading:
Iron City No. 1 Power Generator and Compute Center sits on Paul Hoffman Road outside Karthaus, in Clearfield County, Pennsylvania, an area long shaped by the region's coal and natural gas industry. The facility's own name describes its function directly: on-site power generation paired with computing hardware, the standard behind-the-meter arrangement used by cryptocurrency mining operations that draw on stranded or otherwise hard-to-sell electricity rather than buying power from the regional grid the way conventional data centers do. Clearfield County has old coal seams, associated methane, and gas wells that have drawn this kind of flexible, power-hungry compute load in recent years, since mining rigs can absorb electrical output that would otherwise go unused or unsold.

No operator name, fuel source, or hardware count for this specific site could be confirmed through public filings, local news coverage, or an operator website. This listing should be read as a cryptocurrency mining and hosting site built around its own generation rather than a conventional enterprise data center, and it will be updated if a named operator, permit filing, or news account of the site becomes available. No capacity or size figures are published here because none could be verified.
